learning_outcomes.text: Students know a declarative programming language.
Students can recognize and apply abstraction in program development.
Students can distinguish different programming paradigms and their application areas.
Students have knowledge in testing and verification of programs.
Students know the mathematical foundations of declarative programming.
Students can follow scientific working methods (recognizing, formulating, solving problems, training abstraction skills).
Students are able to speak freely about scientific content, both in front of an audience and in a discussion.

syllabus_topics: Introduction to declarative programming: Fundamental concepts
Proof of program properties (Equational Reasoning, Induction techniques)

assessment_methods.method: Weekly exercises, at least 50% of points
Oral presentation of solutions for at least two exercises

assessment_rules: To acquire credit points, students must achieve at least 50 percent of the points from the weekly exercises and orally present the solution to at least two exercises. The grading is done on a scale of 0 to 15 points according to the examination regulations for the B.Sc. Computer Science degree program.
bibliography: M. Felleisen, R. B. Findler, M. Flatt, S. Krishnamurthi: How to Design Programs, Second Edition, MIT Press 2014
L.Sterling, E.Shapiro: The Art of Prolog, MIT Press 1994
